title: Will and Ledger
premise: When estate lawyer Coral Delacroix is handed a will naming a beneficiary who officially died ten years ago, they assume it's fraud — until the town founder's exhumed coffin proves empty and the will's signatures begin matching documents Coral themselves filed years ago. Hunting the 'dead' witness, Ada Voss, forces Coral to confront the ledger of secrets they've kept for the town's powerful families, including their own complicity in burying what happened a decade ago. The witness was never dead; she's been living as the town's quiet archivist, gathering proof that the founder faked his death to escape justice for a fatal fire he set. In the end, Coral must choose between the law that made their career and the truth, testifying to break open the founder's surviving empire at the cost of their own license.
about_author: Vesper Crane is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent seven years filing wills, deeds, and the occasional document no one wanted found. They write mysteries about paper trails, quiet towns, and the people paid to keep both orderly.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't Filed
chapters.summary: Coral Delacroix's POV. A stranger leaves an unsigned, undated will on Coral's desk naming Ada Voss — declared dead ten years ago — as beneficiary of founder Edmund Hale's estate. Coral recognizes the handwriting as Hale's own. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into dread as Coral realizes the document predates Hale's funeral.

chapters.title: Exhumation
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A court order — filed by an anonymous petitioner — forces Hale's exhumation before the will can be probated. The coffin is empty except for a ledger page bearing Coral's own notarized stamp from nine years ago. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past Coral alphabetized has come unfiled.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Alphabetical Silence
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with flashback fragments. Coral reviews their decade of estate work for the Hale family and realizes how many 'closed' files involved the 2015 mill fire that killed three workers. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing; Coral begins pulling copies they were never supposed to keep.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Maren, the town historical society's soft-spoken archivist, who warns Coral off certain records with unsettling precision. Coral notices Maren's knowledge of the fire matches no public record. Emotional beat: suspicion mixed with reluctant kinship between two keepers of secrets.

chapters.title: Hale's Heirs
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The Hale children — councilman Julian and philanthropist Ruth — pressure Coral to declare the will fraudulent, offering partnership and veiled threats. Someone ransacks Coral's office overnight but takes only one folder: the fire settlement. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Fire Ate
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals she survived the mill fire under a different name; Ada Voss was her sister, who died covering up Edmund Hale's arson. She's been assembling evidence ever since, and the will was her trap. Emotional beat: grief and resolve; the 'dead witness' asks Coral to finish what the law wouldn't.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The ledger page from the coffin matches pages held by Julian Hale — proof the family knew the grave was empty. Coral confronts Julian, who offers immunity in exchange for the original will. Emotional beat: temptation; power makes its offer politely, then less so.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren's archive is set ablaze; she barely escapes with the core evidence, and Coral shelters her, becoming a target themselves. The town's sheriff, long on Hale retainer, issues a warrant for Coral's arrest on fabricated charges. Emotional beat: point of no return; allies now fugitives together.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the emergency hearing, Coral abandons defense strategy and puts Maren on the stand, entering the ledger, the empty-coffin photographs, and Hale's signed confession draft into record while Julian's counsel implodes. Emotional beat: climax; Coral burns their career as fuel for the truth.

chapters.title: Closing Entries
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, months later. Hale's estate is dissolved, Julian indicted, and Coral, disbarred but unrepentant, opens a records clinic helping townspeople read their own buried histories. Maren signs the final page of her sister's file. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; justice outside the law still costs, but it holds.
